A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ALEXR framework, convergence analysis and lower-bound constructions. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison after matching moved and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical results, analytical complexity comparisons and illustrations of lower-bound constructions. Neither its main text nor its appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: Section 9 reports original GDRO and partial-AUC experiments in Figures 1–2 and Tables 4–5. Appendix F adds dataset analysis and an empirical investigation of the theoretical sparsity term.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains identical extrapolation, block-coordinate dual updates, independent inner batches and primal updates. The new applications instantiate the existing ALEXR procedure. The modified SOTA algorithm is an experimental comparator, not a change to ALEXR.

E1.justification: v1 presents motivating applications without evaluating datasets. v2 adds CVaR-GDRO experiments on Adult and CelebA, and restricted-TPR partial-AUC experiments on Covtype, Higgs, Cardiomegaly and Lung-mass, introducing empirical coverage across tabular, face-image and medical-image tasks.

E2.justification: v2 introduces actual empirical comparisons against BSGD, SOX, SONX, OOA, SGD and SGD-UW for GDRO. The pAUC comparison includes BSGD, SOX, SONX, OOA, an adapted SOTA and oversampled cross-entropy training. These comparisons were absent from v1; the theoretical comparator sets in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new experiments introduce held-out splits, linear prediction models, fixed iteration budgets and evaluation using worst-fraction group accuracy and restricted-TPR pAUC. Appendix F specifies 64 samples per GDRO iteration and 16 positive plus 16 negative samples per pAUC iteration. These are new protocols, not revisions to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix F.1.3 and Figure 3 add focused checks of rare-group populations and whether empirical Omega_Y^0 is substantially below its worst-case bound. The theoretical comparison with extrapolation disabled already existed in v1 Appendix G and is retained as v2 Appendix H.

E5.justification: v2 introduces five runs with different random seeds for both experimental suites, ± summaries in Tables 4–5 and shaded bands in Figures 1–2. v1 has no corresponding empirical uncertainty reporting. The PDFs do not define whether the ± values or bands represent standard deviations, standard errors or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: v2 adds convergence curves, test scores and sparsity diagnostics absent from v1. For example, ALEXR obtains 56.58±0.69% Adult accuracy at alpha=0.1 and 0.727±0.003 Covtype pAUC at TPR≥0.5. It has the highest reported central score in four of eight GDRO settings and is best or tied in seven of eight pAUC settings.

T1.justification: The main convergence rates and lower bounds remain unchanged. v2 adds the pAUC reformulations in Equations (2.3)–(2.5), revises norm and smoothness definitions, and corrects factors in the retained Theorem 22 proof, including the 1/n factor in (H.4). The former SOX-labelled analysis is restricted in attribution to ALEXR with theta=0.

C1.justification: The conclusion now explicitly includes restricted-TPR pAUC and claims promising empirical performance on GDRO and pAUC. The central contributions—single-loop optimization, improved convergence rates, minibatch speedup and matching lower bounds—retain their original scope.

C2.justification: Section 9 adds interpretations favoring group-aware optimization over ERM/up-weighting and pAUC surrogate optimization over cross-entropy in the tested settings. Section 5.1 also replaces v1's claimed SOX objective-gap guarantee with an explicit statement that such a guarantee remains absent for non-strongly-convex SOX.

D1.justification: New Appendix F documents PyTorch, CPU hardware, preprocessing, group construction, feature extraction, tuning grids and regularization. It specifies pretrained ResNet18 features for CelebA and provides a pointer to the projection implementation used for OOA. v1 contains no comparable experimental implementation documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds AUC, consistency, class-imbalance and dataset references. Its STORM citation changes from Cutkosky–Mehta in v1 to a different Cutkosky–Orabona work in v2, and the relationship to SOX is qualified. Most existing related-work discussion and theoretical positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Applications becomes a standalone section, the single-loop discussion moves within related work, and the theta=0 appendix is retitled. The title and abstract switch from an algorithm family to a singular algorithm. New experimental sections extend the narrative, while most retained exposition remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 adds a substantial empirical presentation: multipanel convergence plots in Figures 1–2, group-size and sparsity diagnostics in Figure 3, result Tables 4–5 and dataset-statistics Table 6. Original complexity Tables 1–3 and the Appendix E function illustrations are retained, with some displays relocated.

improvement.justification: v1 supports its applications analytically; v2 makes practical usefulness assessable through comparative convergence curves, held-out results, five-seed runs, implementation details and an empirical sparsity check. This substantially strengthens the evidence while retaining the principal theoretical results. Undefined uncertainty summaries and a max/min inconsistency in the new Equation (2.4) limit clarity, and the GDRO rankings support a qualified performance conclusion, but these issues do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and reproducibility.
